Tiêu đề đề bài: Task 2.1: Children Using Smartphones at an Early Age
Nội dung chi tiết:
Read the following statement:

"An increasing number of children are being given smartphones from a very young age. While some people believe that early access to smartphones brings educational and communication benefits, others are concerned about its negative effects on children's health, concentration, and social skills."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing the advantages and disadvantages of children using smartphones from an early age. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.
title: Task 2.1: Children Using Smartphones at an Early Age
content:
Read the following statement:

"An increasing number of children are being given smartphones from a very young age. While some people believe that early access to smartphones brings educational and communication benefits, others are concerned about its negative effects on children's health, concentration, and social skills."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing the advantages and disadvantages of children using smartphones from an early age. Support your arguments with specific reasons and illustrative examples.

body1.example: For instance, my brother was worried about his young daughter falling behind in English speaking at primary school. Therefore, he decided to let her use a fun English app on his smartphone for 20 minutes every evening. As a result, he finally saw her pronounce new words clearly and enjoy studying. If he had not used that learning tool, she would not have been so confident in class.
body1.focus: Advantages: Educational support and quick communication
body1.frame: Mở: On the one hand, children using smartphones at an early age brings a lot of advantages in several ways | Ruột ĐOẠN 1 | Chốt: Clearly, these benefits make early smartphone use appealing to many people.
body1.point: A very important point to consider is that smartphones help children make the most of new technology to broaden their mind. This means that young students can use educational apps to practice English, watch science clips, and receive instant feedback on their mistakes. Another point I would like to make is that phones make family communication fast and convenient. This is because of the fact that busy parents can easily call or check on their children right after school.

body2.example: For example, I was shocked when I stayed at my aunt's house and saw her eight-year-old son play mobile games until midnight. For this reason, I got to help him join a local football club so he could play outside with friends. If I had not seen his tired eyes every morning, I would not have been able to know that too much screen time harms children's health and focus so fast.
body2.focus: Disadvantages: Health problems, poor concentration, and weak social skills
body2.frame: Mở: On the other hand, the disadvantages of children using smartphones at an early age are undeniable | Ruột ĐOẠN 2 | Chốt: It is clear that health and focus problems can create serious drawbacks if ignored.
body2.point: In fact, spending too many hours on smartphones harms children's health and weakens their concentration at school. This happens because when young children lack proper guidance and self-control, it easily leads to eye strain, watching violent videos, and copying bad habits from the internet. In addition, staring at screens all evening reduces face-to-face interaction with family members and classmates.

hint.conclusion: In conclusion, children using smartphones at an early age brings both pros and cons. While people can benefit from educational apps and quick parent-child communication, they also need to handle eye strain, poor concentration, and weak social skills. Therefore, both individuals and schools should work together to make the most of smartphone use for children responsibly.

Tiêu đề đề bài: Task 1.2: Replying to Alex About the Upcoming Trip to Scotland
Nội dung chi tiết:
You have received an email from your friend, Alex, regarding your upcoming trip to Scotland together. Read part of his email below:

"I am super excited about our upcoming trip to Scotland! First, when would you like to depart? Second, do you agree with traveling there by train, and what transport should we use to get around once we are in Scotland? Also, we will be staying at my uncle's house in the mountains—do you worry there might be a lack of entertainment or interesting places to visit nearby?"

Write an informal email responding to Alex.
title: Task 1.2: Replying to Alex About the Upcoming Trip to Scotland
content:
You have received an email from your friend, Alex, regarding your upcoming trip to Scotland together. Read part of his email below:

"I am super excited about our upcoming trip to Scotland! First, when would you like to depart? Second, do you agree with traveling there by train, and what transport should we use to get around once we arrive in Scotland? Also, we will be staying at my uncle's house in the mountains—do you worry there might be a lack of entertainment or interesting places to visit nearby?"

Write an informal email responding to Alex.

body.answer: I would like to let you know that I prefer leaving on Saturday morning around 8 a.m.
body.example: We can finish packing on Friday night and catch an early train without rushing.
body.reason: This departure time fits comfortably within my daily routine and gives us enough time to arrive before dark.

body.answer: From my point of view, I think that traveling there by train is a great idea.
body.example: We can chat, listen to music, or look out the window at the countryside during the ride.
body.reason: Taking the train is fast, convenient for busy people, and allows us to relax comfortably instead of driving a long distance.

body.answer: I believe we should use local buses and trains to move between towns, and walk around small villages.
body.example: We can take a local bus from the station to nearby sights and walk along the scenic trails.
body.reason: Public transport is affordable, helps protect the environment, and lets us stay on the safe side without worrying about driving on narrow mountain roads.
body.requirement: What transport to use to get around once arriving in Scotland

body.answer: I think that staying at your uncle's mountain house will be wonderful, so I am not worried about a lack of entertainment at all.
body.example: We can go hiking in the fresh air during the day, visit nearby villages, and play board games or cook dinner together at night.
body.reason: Being in crowded, noisy public venues easily makes people feel stressed, whereas a mountain house offers a quiet, cozy environment that is beneficial to our physical and mental health.
body.requirement: Whether you worry about a lack of entertainment or places to visit near his uncle's house in the mountains

Tiêu đề đề bài: Task 2.2: Advantages and Disadvantages of Working in Public Places
Nội dung chi tiết:
Read the following statement:

"Nowadays, many people prefer working or studying in public places such as coffee shops, libraries, or coworking spaces instead of working in traditional offices or at home."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing both the advantages and disadvantages of working in public places. Include specific reasons and examples from your knowledge or experience to support your arguments.
title: Task 2.2: Advantages and Disadvantages of Working in Public Places
content:
Read the following statement:

"Nowadays, many people prefer working or studying in public places such as coffee shops, libraries, or coworking spaces instead of working in traditional offices or at home."

Write an essay to an educated reader discussing both the advantages and disadvantages of working in public places. Include specific reasons and examples from your knowledge or experience to support your arguments.

body1.example: For instance, my brother was feeling bored and sleepy when working alone in his small bedroom every day. Therefore, he decided to work at a coworking space near his house three times a week. As a result, he finally finished his design projects faster and met friendly freelancers. If he had not tried working in a public space, he would not have been so creative and motivated.
body1.focus: Advantages: Convenient facilities and social connection
body1.frame: Mở: On the one hand, working or studying in public places brings a lot of advantages in several ways | Ruột ĐOẠN 1 | Chốt: Clearly, these benefits make working in public places appealing to many people.
body1.point: A very important point to consider is that cafes, libraries, and coworking spaces are fast, convenient for busy people in modern-day society. This means that workers and students can easily enjoy comfortable seating, air conditioning, and stable internet without paying office rent. Another point I would like to make is that public spaces help people stay motivated and build social connections. This is because of the fact that seeing others study or work hard boosts energy and lets people meet like-minded people.

body2.example: For example, I was trying to prepare an important presentation at a crowded coffee shop last weekend. For this reason, I got to move back to my quiet room at home because loud phone calls kept breaking my focus. If I had not had that frustrating afternoon, I would not have been able to know that noisy venues and public Wi-Fi are risky for serious work.
body2.focus: Disadvantages: Noise, extra costs, and lack of privacy
body2.frame: Mở: On the other hand, the disadvantages of working or studying in public places are undeniable | Ruột ĐOẠN 2 | Chốt: It is clear that noise distractions and privacy risks can create serious drawbacks if ignored.
body2.point: In fact, crowded, noisy public venues easily make people feel stressed and lose concentration. This happens because when other customers talk loudly or play music nearby, it easily leads to mistakes and slower work performance. In addition, buying drinks every day costs a great deal of money, and using public Wi-Fi lacks personal privacy when handling private files.

hint.conclusion: In conclusion, working or studying in public places brings both pros and cons. While people can benefit from convenient facilities and social energy, they also need to handle noise distractions, extra daily costs, and privacy risks. Therefore, both individuals and companies should work together to make the most of working in public places responsibly.
